Class BattleView

java.lang.Object
javafx.scene.Node
javafx.scene.Parent
javafx.scene.layout.Region
javafx.scene.layout.Pane
javafx.scene.layout.BorderPane
gamemode.fightscene.BattleView
All Implemented Interfaces:
javafx.css.Styleable, javafx.event.EventTarget
public class BattleView extends javafx.scene.layout.BorderPane
Represents the graphical battle interface between the player and a dinosaur enemy.

This class renders the full battle scene including the background, enemy sprite and HP, player sprite and HP, and the CommandBox for battle actions.

Communication with the rest of the game is done via BattleCallback, which is implemented by GameController in production and by a simple stub in tests. This removes the hard dependency on the GameController singleton and makes the class fully testable.

Layout

 BorderPane (BattleView)
 ├── CENTER — StackPane (battleArea)
 │   ├── ImageView background
 │   └── AnchorPane spriteLayer
 │       ├── VBox enemyGroup   (top-right)
 │       └── VBox playerGroup  (bottom-left)
 └── BOTTOM — CommandBox

  • Constructor Details

    • BattleView

      public BattleView(Dinosaur enemy, GameController controller)
      Production constructor — accepts the real GameController.

      GameController is adapted to BattleCallback inline so no changes are needed in GameController itself.

      Parameters:
      enemy - the enemy dinosaur encountered in battle
      controller - the singleton game controller

    • BattleView

      public BattleView(Dinosaur enemy, BattleCallback callback)
      Testable constructor — accepts any BattleCallback implementation.

      Use this constructor in unit tests to pass a lightweight stub without needing to construct or subclass the GameController singleton.

      Parameters:
      enemy - the enemy dinosaur encountered in battle
      callback - the callback that handles battle outcomes
